From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-demo MAP: Ownership & turnaround for MSA/DPA/SLA redlines

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Per our shared MAP template, I wanted to capture the legal milestones and who will drive each step so we can hit the target close date (2026-09-10). Please confirm or correct any ownership/ETAs below.

Summary (agreed on call)
- Target close date: 2026-09-10 (commercial + legal signoff)
- MAP milestone in scope for legal: initial redlines (MSA/DPA), SLA threshold adjustments, and final signoff.

Proposed ownership & turnaround (draft):
1) First-pass redlines (MSA/DPA): ACME legal to return redlines to Redwood by 2026-08-27 EOD (primary input: legal team).
2) Redwood legal (Lauren) to review ACME redlines and return counter-redlines by 2026-08-30 (48–72 business hours after receipt).
3) Commercial reconciliation (Marcus + Jordan) to agree on compromise terms by 2026-09-02 and capture in MAP.
4) Final SLA appendix and annex signoff: target 2026-09-07 for signatures to allow e-signing buffer.

Dependencies: proof of SOC2 report (ACME requested), appendix with data retention settings, and any additional security scoping questions. I attached a draft MAP (draft_map_v2.xlsx) and a starter redline (redline_msa_v1.docx) for reference.

Open ask for ACME: can your legal commit to the 08/27 turnaround? If not, propose an alternate date so we can adjust the MAP. Also confirm whether ACME prefers to own the first redline or would like Redwood to propose language for any high-risk clauses (data residency, audit rights).

Next steps (internal): Marcus — can you confirm commercial priorities (discount vs SLA priorities) so I can flag negotiables to Lauren?
Lauren — please confirm your typical review SLA and whether we can compress review time if ACME provides clean redlines.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Thanks for the context, team. I reviewed the draft redline stub you attached. Proposed internal process (to minimize turn-around):

1) When ACME provides their redlines, please upload them to our shared folder and ping me directly. I will perform a triage within 24 business hours to categorize comments as: commercial, security, or non-substantive.
2) For commercial items, I'll coordinate with Marcus and provide suggested compromise language within 48 business hours of triage.
3) Security or privacy items that require product input will be routed to the security SLA queue (typically adds 3 business days depending on clarity).
4) If ACME wants Redwood to propose the SLA annex language, I can supply a Redwood-first draft same day we receive the redlines (or sooner) — that should shorten back-and-forth.

Turnaround commitments I can make now:
- Acknowledgement on receipt: same day.
- Full first counter (where feasible): within 48–72 business hours after ACME submission.

If ACME moves their first redline to 08/28, our target timeline becomes:
- ACME redlines in: 2026-08-28
- Redwood counter: 2026-09-01
- Commercial signoff window: 2026-09-01 -> 2026-09-05
- Final signatures: aim for 2026-09-08 -> 2026-09-10 (still achievable)

I will also prepare a simple "legal ownership" column in the MAP spreadsheet that maps each clause to the owner, ETA, and escalation contact. That will be shared to the HubSpot deal record and the folder linked below.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
